Variants.Content: How a Free City views outsiders often says more about its character than official etiquette. Outsiders bring goods and news, so they are both welcome and wary; cities use taxes, licenses and contracts to mark out places for strangers; trade routes, marriage alliances and wars will continually force this judgment to change.

Entry Outsiders in the Free Cities How a Free City views outsiders often says more about its character than official etiquette. Outsiders bring goods and news, so they are both welcome and wary; cities use taxes, licenses and contracts to mark out places for strangers; trade routes, marriage alliances and wars Whether it is valid depends on who can grant the rights, collect the consideration, and actually make the judgment come to fruition in the event of default.
